title: Rigidity of cartesian smooth comparisons of labeled ordinary towers
statement: Let L be linearly ordered, X and Y schemes, h:Y to X a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and A and B intrinsic labeled ordinary towers on X and Y [def-trf-intrinsic-labeled-resolution]. The type of contracted cartesian comparisons of B with A over h is a subsingleton: any two natural transformations with the specified cartesian squares, extended center ideals and retained labels agree, including all structure fields.

source.place: VIII 2.1.1--2.1.9, 2.3.1, 2.3.4--2.3.5, 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.86--88,91--94. Agent expansion of the conditional embedded-to-intrinsic argument, not a separately quoted ILO theorem.

proof.text: Take two comparisons c and d. Index the towers by the union of their finite active label sets. The stage isomorphisms and index_labels identify all cuts between successive labels with one numbered stage. At the initial cut, the cartesian square equation and the initial isomorphisms force the component to be the conjugate of h. Thus c and d agree initially.

Suppose the components agree before an active target label. Naturality gives two lifts of the same morphism into its next ordinary blowup. By either comparison cartesian square at the next cut, the map into this blowup is a base change of h and is smooth [lem-pc-proper-base-change], hence flat [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]. The exceptional ideal is invertible [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], so its pullback along this flat map is invertible. (Locally, tensor the injection of a rank-one invertible ideal into the structure ring with a flat algebra.) Consequently the uniqueness part of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property], hom_ext_of_isInvertible_comap, makes the two lifts equal.

An absent target label has an isomorphism as transition, so cancellation gives the next equality. The retained clauses forbid a source label outside the target labels. Continue the finite induction, then use the stage isomorphisms to get equality at every cut and natural-transformation extensionality to get c.map=d.map. The other fields are proofs, so proof irrelevance gives c=d. If both towers have length zero the initial step already proves everything.

lean.statement:
theorem intrinsic_resolution_pullback_subsingleton
    {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : Y ⟶ X) [Smooth h]
    (A : IntrinsicLabeledOrdinaryTower L X) (B : IntrinsicLabeledOrdinaryTower L Y) :
    Subsingleton (IntrinsicLabeledResolutionPullback h A B)
